items.text: WTI +1.8% and Brent +3.0% WoW amid Middle East tensions; crude has sustained strength after Iran conflict resumed in July. Oil-sensitive credits and commodity hedgers face pressure, while refiners and energy credits benefit—watch for spread widening in energy-linked corporates if prices hold above $85.

July payrolls collapsed -23K (vs +20K June), reversing a multi-month positive streak and signaling unexpected deterioration. Unemployment held 4.1%, claims remain moderate at 206K, but breadth of the payroll miss is a red flag for recession-sensitive credits and high-beta equity-linked debt.

Headline CPI cooled to 3.3%, core PCE to 2.47%, and PPI fell to 4.66%—all trending down. However, year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 4.3% (Aug prelim) as geopolitical risk priced in. Sticky service inflation (PCE core still above 2%) and pricing power in ISM Services (70.3) remain concerns for high-yield spreads.

Fed funds flat at 3.75%; 10Y Treasury at 4.74% (up 2bp WoW) amid curve flattening (2-10 curve 46bp vs 52bp prior). ECB held rates at 2.25% deposit facility in July; September tightening now fully priced. Volatility in rates creates refi risk and mark-to-market pressure on duration-laden credit portfolios.

HY OAS tightened 4bp to 269bp; IG OAS flat at 81bp; CCC OAS widened 6bp to 1036bp. Bifurcation continues—lower tier and distressed names losing technical support as growth doubts mount. Refinancing wall risk elevated for weaker BB/B issuers amid higher yields and payroll shock.

GDPNow jumped to 4.03% (from 1.54%), but Q2 actual GDP at only 1.5% (down from 2.1% Q1) signals deceleration despite nowcast strength. Retail sales declined -0.6% m/m in July after months of resilience; ex-autos down -0.3%. Consumer demand cooling into late summer—special situations investors should watch Q3 earnings guidance for forward demand signals.

Michigan sentiment collapsed to 51.0 (prelim Aug) from 55.2, the sharpest one-month drop since May peak; expectations down 11-17%. Housing weakness: existing home sales down to 4.06M SAAR (July), starts down to 1.239M. VIX at 15.85, still calm but sentiment deterioration + retail miss + payroll shock = recipe for credit widening if consumer narrative breaks further.

themeCards.title: Labor Market Deterioration
themeCards.statusLine: July payroll print of -23K reversed momentum after six consecutive months of gains, sparking first major recession signal of the cycle. Unemployment static at 4.1%, claims ticking up; breadth of miss suggests demand shock rather than supply rebalance.
themeCards.relevance: Payroll shock is a high-beta trigger for credit widening, especially in consumer-discretionary, travel, and leisure-dependent credits. Refinancing windows for weaker issuers narrows materially if labor market deteriorates further—watch August payroll print (due 9/5) as make-or-break for credit valuations.

themeCards.title: Consumer Demand & Confidence Cliff
themeCards.statusLine: Retail sales fell -0.6% m/m (July) after months of resilience; Michigan consumer sentiment plunged 8% to 51 (Aug prelim), ending two-month rebound. Sentiment now 12% below year-ago; only 8% of consumers expect income to outpace inflation.
themeCards.relevance: Consumer soft landing narrative is cracking. For special situations, watch for fallen angels in discretionary retail, auto finance, and leveraged consumer credit. Expect spread widening in sub-investment-grade consumer-exposed sectors and higher default rates in RMBS/ABS if sentiment doesn't recover by September.

themeCards.title: Geopolitical Risk & Oil Shock Pass-Through
themeCards.statusLine: Brent +3% WoW to $95.29; WTI +1.8% to $86.48 following July Iran escalation. Year-ahead inflation expectations spiked to 4.3% (Aug); long-term expectations anchored at 3.3%. Energy pass-through creating margin pressure and pricing uncertainty.
themeCards.relevance: Direct hits to transport, logistics, chemicals, and rate-sensitive sectors. Second-order effects via services pricing (ISM Services prices at 70.3, highest since Aug 2022) threaten margin compression in leveraged companies. Energy hedging costs have risen—watch energy-linked CDS and refinancing spreads for mid-cap energy and shipping credits.

themeCards.title: Credit Market Bifurcation & CCC Stress
themeCards.statusLine: CCC OAS widened 6bp to 1036bp; HY OAS only 269bp despite payroll shock; duration of tightness suggests technical exhaustion. IG OAS flat at 81bp masks rising rate sensitivity and refinancing cliff for lower-tier BB/B cohort due Sept–Nov.
themeCards.relevance: Historically, CCC widening coupled with IG stability signals liquidity bifurcation and forced selling ahead. For special situations, this is prime hunting ground: distressed credits trading below intrinsic; refi wall risks for 2026–2027 maturities; and potential technical capitulation if payroll data deteriorates further.

themeCards.title: China Growth & Export Demand Weakness
themeCards.statusLine: China NBS Manufacturing PMI at 49.2 (July), marking contraction below 50; new orders weak, export orders collapsing. Non-manufacturing also below 50 at 49.0. Signals soft landing gone awry, demand destruction, and spillover risk to global growth.
themeCards.relevance: Hits directly to commodity, industrial-metals, and supply-chain credits; China-exposed multinationals facing margin pressure. Watch for credit downgrades in mid-cycle industrials dependent on China capex stimulus. For US credits, China slowdown reduces global risk appetite and could trigger portfolio rotations into safety.

themeCards.title: Refinancing Wall & Curve Steepening Risk
themeCards.statusLine: 2-10 curve at 46bp (flattening from 52bp); 10Y Treasury at 4.74%, up 2bp WoW; curve inversion persists. Massive refi calendar for BB/B credits due Sept–Dec 2026; higher rates + payroll shock = markedly wider refi spreads and potential issuance freezes.
themeCards.relevance: This is the month-to-month risk most material to special situations: fallen angels, turnarounds, and distressed refi candidates all face materially higher issuance costs. For investors, this creates dislocation opportunities—watch for secondary bid-ask dislocations in 2026 maturity bonds and high-yield issues from non-investment-grade issuers facing Sept–Oct maturities.

regime.label: Late-cycle deceleration
regime.detail: payroll shock + consumer cliff, flattening curve, geopolitical oil premium, bifurcating credit, CCC stress emerging
